name: New Orleans by Night Coteries & Factions (Lore)

text.content: Marcel keeps his mansion open to favored guests — officially out of hospitality, but really to watch them closely and bind them in debt. Current permanent residents include his childer Christopher and Anthony, the mysterious painter Josua Cambridge, and Marie D'Richet, whose body lies guarded in extended torpor. Rivalries simmer constantly beneath a veneer of politeness, particularly between the rebellious Christopher and the ever-devoted Anthony, each vying for their sire's favor.

Formed by Prince Doran in 1841 after crushing an anarch arson plot at the City Exchange, the Council of five elders was meant to advise New Orleans' prince. Its surviving members — Karen Chartry, Dutch, Sebastian Walcott and Avery — now spend more effort undermining Marcel's decrees than supporting them, quietly issuing their own “suggestions” to the city's Kindred. Karen Chartry has become its unofficial leader in all but name. The Toreador Morgaine pointedly refuses membership, and Avery participates only occasionally, both facts that weaken the Council's unity.

Formed in the 1960s after Marcel began evicting refugee Kindred to curb overcrowding, the Underground Society publicly helps newcomers settle in New Orleans while privately serving as a power base for Dutch and Marcel's own childe Christopher. Its members, terrified of losing their tenuous place in the city, play the game of prestation as devoutly as any Harpy, hoping their favors will be repaid with permission to stay.

An anarch cabal responsible for the 1841 City Exchange fire and decades of assassinations against New Orleans' elders, the Phoenix Society takes its calling card from Prince's song “7”, played on local radio to announce an impending strike. Its true goal is the destruction of the Justicars, whom it blames for generations of anarch persecution; it has twice targeted Justicar Xaviar during his triennial Conclaves. Marcel knows only two of its members by identity — a leader called General and an operative called B — and suspects quiet support from Setites and the mage Martin D'Richet.

Justicar Xaviar's personal cell of spies, the Tabula Rasa watches the caern hidden in New Orleans on his behalf. Its five members — James “Teddy” Lugor, Kendrick McKenin, Lane Nassam, Miguel Salmararez and Elzra Taliano — are former police officers recruited for narrow, dangerous specialties (explosives, survivalism, surveillance, and the like); Lugor and Taliano are ghouls, the rest mortal. Taliano, a former N.O.S.T.F. staker Blood Bound after her recruitment, nurses a private grudge against Detective Robert Carter, whose indifference to her drove her from his task force and into Xaviar's service.

pages.name: Justicar Xaviar and the Swamp Festival Conclave

text.content: Xaviar, Gangrel Justicar for the past century, convenes a Conclave in New Orleans every three years to coincide with the city's Swamp Festival, ostensibly to review the old Kindred–Lupine land treaty. His true purpose is a hidden, abandoned caern near the more famous Bayou St. John caern, apparently once used by werecreatures other than the Uktena; Xaviar has spent decades secretly siphoning its power through his personal spy cell, the Tabula Rasa, taking care never to visit the city more often than the Conclave allows so as not to raise suspicion.

pages.name: The New Orleans Special Task Force (N.O.S.T.F.)

text.content: Founded by the vengeful ex-ghoul Detective Robert Carter, the N.O.S.T.F. is a cell of 16 specially recruited officers operating within the N.O.P.D. but loyal only to Carter. Under a truce first struck with Prince Doran and renewed with Marcel, the Task Force may hunt vampires who endanger the Masquerade or refuse to Present themselves to the prince, in exchange for otherwise leaving the city's Kindred population alone. Carter would gladly break the truce and purge the city of the Damned entirely, given the opportunity.

Few New Orleans Kindred can say for certain that Jereaux, Prince Marcel's older brother and sire's-childe, still exists, for he has not been seen in Kindred society since shortly after Marcel's coronation. In truth Jereaux, embraced during the Civil War by the elder Lothar Constantine (whom the brothers later disposed of together), quietly orchestrated Marcel's rise to the throne after Doran's murder and continues to act as his brother's hidden enforcer from the family plantation, Rubis d'le Nuit. Whenever Marcel suspects a serious threat, he brings the matter to Jereaux rather than act openly, keeping his own hands clean of the outcome.

pages.name: The Setites of New Orleans and the Voodoo Cults

text.content: Barred from the city since Prince Doran's earliest days, the Followers of Set gained a foothold in New Orleans through the Voodoo cults brought by the slave trade from Haiti in the 1700s and 1800s, dominating many cults' Voodoo Queens and Witch Doctors through Domination or Blood Bonds. The mortal Voodoo Queen Marie Laveau broke much of their hold for over 40 years before age claimed her, after which the cults fractured again and the Setites regained ground. Today the clan's most powerful local representative is Manon, Embraced by the loa-avatar vampire Ghede in Haiti and exiled to New Orleans after a confrontation with her erstwhile mistress Ezuli; Manon runs her temple from the Lakeside Hotel and maintains an uneasy alliance with the Black Spiral Dancers in the western bayous.

pages.name: Cajun Country and the Black Spiral Dancers

text.content: West of New Orleans lies Cajun Country (Acadiana), a region the city's Kindred avoid entirely. Driven from Acadia in 1755, a Hive of Black Spiral Dancers settled in the bayous after being forced west by the Uktena, corrupting several caerns to the Wyrm's purposes ever since. Pentex's Endron International has spread pollution along the Mississippi from a base near Baton Rouge since the 1920s, driving out the Mokole (werealligators) and Gurahl (werebears) who once shared the swamps. Only the self-proclaimed Malkavian/Black Spiral Dancer hybrid Uriah Travers survives there uncorrupted, hated by the Dancers he once called kin and trusted, in his fashion, by the local wererats.

vtmlarp.source: New Orleans by Night, Chapters One & Five
